title: 16 Oct rule change lets AI write deliverable text as [AI] suggestions; 13 IPS rewrites already drafted and public
problem: The team leader's 16 Oct rule lets Claude put [AI]-labelled suggestions into the IPS, Trading Notes and Final Report, with accepted AI wording credited later in the Final Report's Works Cited. Wharton does allow cited AI material, and the IPS instructions send IPS sources to the Final Report, so this is not a clear breach on paper. But AI sentences mixed into the IPS would be judged as the team's own voice ('they must use their voice and words'; 'authentic team voice'), with no credit visible until 4 Dec. About six of the 13 drafted rows add new AI sentences (rows 2, 6, 7, 10, 12, 13). The rest are cuts or number updates. The public history shows the stricter rule was relaxed on purpose.

verifier_note: Evidence checked: caplet-latest/CLAUDE.md:27-30, COMPETITION.md:142-144, IPS_v5_suggestions.md:7-21 exist as quoted. Two corrections. (1) 'No credit at all' is wrong: the IPS instructions route IPS sources to the Final Report on purpose ('sources do not need to be cited in the IPS. Relevant sources and supporting evidence must be included in the Final Report', IPS-FINAL.txt:124-125), and Rules & Roles allows cited AI material ('If you include material generated by an AI program, it should be cited like any other reference material'). So credit is late, not missing, and the plan is not a clear breach on paper. (2) Not all 13 rows are AI wording: rows 3 and 8 are cuts, row 9 is a cut-down, and rows 1, 4, 5 and 11 mainly cut words or update numbers. New AI sentences are mainly in rows 2, 6, 7, 10, 12 and 13. Severity lowered from critical to high. The fix is reframed as team options, because the rule is the team leader's call.

title: [AI] suggestions in the live Google Doc would show up under a student's account and lose the [AI] tag when accepted
problem: The rule has Claude write suggestions straight into the team's Google Doc. Google's Docs API makes suggestions through an authorised account ('set the writeMode field ... to SUGGEST'), and a browser agent would also act inside a logged-in account. Either way the suggestion is made under a student's Google identity. Once accepted, the text joins the document, and the '[AI]' label cannot stay in a submitted IPS. Version history would then show AI wording as that student's edit. This weakens the proof the team is relying on for authorship (INT-02's fix: 'keep each student's dated drafts (Doc version history) as proof'). How the 16 Oct suggestions were or will be placed is not recorded (UNVERIFIED). That Docs shows a suggestion under the account that made it is standard Docs behaviour, not tested today (UNVERIFIED).
